title: Cucurella Makes History With Unique Double as Vinícius Jr. Welcomes New Real Madrid Teammate
excerpt: The Spanish left-back became the first player to win both the FIFA Club World Cup and the FIFA World Cup, earning congratulations from his new captain.
body:
• Marc Cucurella became the first player ever to win both the FIFA Club World Cup and the FIFA World Cup after Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina in the 2026 final.
  • Real Madrid captain Vinícius Jr. publicly congratulated and welcomed Cucurella on Instagram, posting: "Congratulations and welcome, Cucu!"
  • Spain conceded just one goal across eight World Cup matches — the fewest by any World Cup-winning side — with Cucurella starting every game at left back.
  • Cucurella joined Real Madrid from Chelsea this summer in a €60 million deal and will report for preseason after a three-week break.

Hours after Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final at MetLife Stadium, Real Madrid captain Vinícius Jr. took to Instagram to welcome his newest teammate. The Brazilian posted a photo of Marc Cucurella kissing the World Cup trophy alongside the caption: "Congratulations and welcome, Cucu!" — the first public interaction between the two players who are expected to form a formidable left-side partnership under José Mourinho next season.

The message capped a summer of historic proportions for the 27-year-old left-back. Real Madrid announced Cucurella's €60 million signing from Chelsea on the same day Spain opened their World Cup campaign, and a month later, the defender lifted the sport's biggest prize.

A Feat No One Has Matched

With Spain's triumph, Cucurella became the first player in football history to win both the modern FIFA Club World Cup and the FIFA World Cup. He was part of the Chelsea squad that lifted the inaugural expanded Club World Cup in the United States last summer. Only one other player — Argentina's Enzo Fernández — had the same opportunity in the final, but Spain's victory meant only Cucurella completed the double.

The distinction matters. While players like Pelé won both the World Cup and the old Intercontinental Cup, FIFA considers the new Club World Cup a separate competition. Cucurella stands alone in this particular record.

Spain's Defensive Wall

Cucurella started every minute of Spain's eight-match World Cup run. Luis de la Fuente's side conceded just one goal across the entire tournament — the fewest by any World Cup-winning team. Belgium were the only side to breach the defence, scoring in the quarter-finals in Los Angeles.

"We've done an incredible job in that regard all tournament, and not just the defenders and the goalkeeper, because I think it's a team effort. Ultimately it's about everyone making sacrifices. We attack together and defend together."

Substitute Ferran Torres delivered the decisive blow, scoring in the second period of extra time to break down a 10-man Argentina at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Spain's second World Cup title — their first since 2010 — sparked celebrations that stretched into Monday morning across Madrid.

Parade Through Madrid

The squad flew home on Monday for a victory parade that wound through the Spanish capital to the Plaza de Cibeles, the traditional epicenter of Spanish football celebrations. Hundreds of thousands of fans lined the avenues as the team, led by manager De la Fuente, received a formal reception at Zarzuela Palace from Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, Queen Letizia, and King Felipe VI before boarding an open-top bus.

Cucurella held up the trophy along the route and grabbed the microphone to sing along to the viral chant using his surname that became a fan anthem during Euro 2024. De la Fuente, meanwhile, reminded Cucurella of a pre-tournament promise: the defender had vowed to get a tattoo of his manager's face if Spain won the title.

What It Means for Real Madrid

Cucurella will take a three-week vacation before joining Real Madrid for preseason. His six-year contract runs until 2031, and the deal — €55 million upfront with €5 million in add-ons — gives Mourinho a battle-tested left-back whose World Cup form reinforced his credentials.

The expectation at the Bernabéu is that Cucurella and Vinícius Jr. will lock down the left flank together. Cucurella's defensive discipline and tireless work rate should allow the Brazilian more freedom in his attacking runs, while the Spaniard's overlapping ability creates additional width.

Cucurella's preseason at Valdebebas is now just weeks away — a new chapter at one of football's most storied clubs, with two world titles already in hand.
